title: Canonical comparison preserves normalized derived open restriction
statement:
Let A be a finite commutative ring, p:V→T a qcqs morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], i:W→T an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], U=V×_T W, k:U→V and r:U→W its projections [def-pc-fibre-product], with r also qcqs. Work in ordinary constant-A module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Write C_X for exact comparison followed by the canonical intrinsic constant-ring realization [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use the canonical open comparison e_j:C_Y j!_e≅j! C_X [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], and the counit-normalized direct-image comparison b_f:C_Y Rf_e≅Rf C_X on bounded-below inputs [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Let a_j:j*_e C_X→C_Y j* be the mate of e_j inverse under the two open adjunctions [prop-exc-open-adjoint]. For K∈D+(U_et,A), let v_K:C_T Rp_e k!_e K≅Rp k! C_U K be b_p followed by Rp(e_k), with the canonical D+ inclusion comparisons inserted. If lam:j*_e Rp_e k!_e K≅Rr_e K has hom equal to the exact unbounded etale exchange at k!_e K [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] followed by Rr_e of the inverse k-open unit, then
C_W(lam.inv) ≫ a_i(Rp_e k!_e K) ≫ i*(v_K.hom) = b_r(K).hom ≫ lambdaInverse(C_U K),
where lambdaInverse is Rr of the k-open unit followed by inverse canonical derived restriction [lem-exc-proetale-derived-open-restriction]. No properness, Noetherian, constructibility, completion, or finite-CD hypothesis occurs.

proof.text: Evaluate the underived restriction of direct image on a test object Q over W. Both paths are sections on V times_T Q, identified with U times_W Q by the Cartesian projections; the constant scalar sections act in the same way. The etale/pro-etale comparison therefore identifies these section maps, and the canonical constant-module realization retains the same scalar action.

proof.text: Use the adjunction of open extension and restriction. Exact open extension implies restriction preserves K-injective complexes. Resolve the open-extended input on V and restrict its resolution on U. Derive the section square of the first step. Its comparison on the two direct-image edges is the counit-normalized comparison, by uniqueness of right derivation. On the D+ input insert the published inclusion comparisons before and after open extension; these are precisely the factors of etaleOriginOpenTargetComparison. Equivalently use the site-comparison exchange identity, transported from left-derived to exact termwise pullback.

proof.text: The unit-normalization theorem identifies the mate of inverse open-extension comparison with the restriction comparison on sheaves. Exact termwise derivation and the canonical realization equivalence preserve this mate and its unit equation. Apply it for both open edges i and k.

proof.text: Apply the square of step 2 to k!K. Its etale restriction followed by Rr applied to the inverse open unit is lam.hom by the supplied equation. On the pro-etale side the corresponding composite is the inverse of the defined lambda inverse. Insert the two unit equations of step 3 and invert the restriction square. Cancel the forward and inverse open units and the D+ compatibility isomorphisms. The remaining factors, in order, are C_W(lam.inv), the mate at Rp_e(k!K), and i* of the target comparison on the left, and b_r followed by the intrinsic lambda inverse on the right. Empty opens and zero coefficients give the same identities in the zero category; no properness or Noetherian hypothesis was used.
